qa_pair.question: Which statement best describes quicksort's pivot-and-partition strategy and its time complexity?

options.A: It repeatedly merges sorted halves, giving O(n log n) time in both the average and worst cases.
options.B: It selects a pivot, partitions the sequence around it, then recursively sorts the partitions; its average time is O(n log n) but its worst case is O(n^2).
options.C: It selects a pivot, partitions the sequence around it, then recursively sorts the partitions; its time is O(n log n) in both the average and worst cases.
options.D: It scans the sequence once, swapping adjacent out-of-order elements, giving O(n^2) time in the average case.

qa_pair.explanation: Quicksort picks a pivot, partitions the sequence so that elements smaller than the pivot come before it and larger elements after it, and then recursively sorts the two partitions. On typical inputs this partitioning splits the data roughly in half at each level, yielding an average time of O(n log n). However, when the pivot repeatedly turns out to be the smallest or largest element (for example, on already-sorted input with a poor pivot choice), the partitions become very unbalanced and the recursion degenerates to O(n^2) in the worst case. Option A describes merge sort, option C wrongly claims the worst case is also O(n log n), and option D describes an adjacent-swap sort such as bubble sort.
qa_pair.concentration: Quicksort's pivot-and-partition strategy and the contrast between its average O(n log n) and worst-case O(n squared) time complexity

qa_pair.question: Unlike quicksort, merge sort is a ____ sorting algorithm, meaning that elements with equal keys keep their original relative order after sorting.
qa_pair.explanation: Merge sort divides the sequence into halves, sorts them recursively, and merges the sorted halves. During the merge step, when two elements have equal keys, the element from the left half is placed first, so equal elements retain their original relative order — the defining property of a stable sort. Quicksort, by contrast, swaps elements across the pivot during partitioning and is not stable in its usual in-place form.
qa_pair.concentration: Merge sort's divide-and-merge approach and its defining properties of stability and O(n) auxiliary space
